note: Holdout #4, written 2026-10-17 20:52 PDT before any run. Expected verdicts from Cochrane, WHO, CDC, NIH, USPSTF, NICE and major reviews. also_ok decided in advance. harmful: shown verdicts that could hurt a reader. None of these claims appear in the regression set, the safety set, the tests, or holdouts #1 to #3.

claims.claim: Colon cancer screening lowers the risk of dying from colon cancer
claims.basis: Cochrane (Hewitson 2007, faecal occult blood test: about 16% fewer colorectal cancer deaths; Holme 2013, sigmoidoscopy: fewer cancers and deaths); USPSTF grade A for ages 50 to 75.

claims.claim: Nicotine patches help people quit smoking
claims.basis: Cochrane (Hartmann-Boyce, nicotine replacement therapy): high-certainty evidence that patches and other forms raise quit rates by roughly 50 to 70%; USPSTF and NICE recommend them.

claims.claim: Exercise helps older people avoid falls
claims.basis: Cochrane (Sherrington 2019): exercise cuts the rate of falls by about 23% in community-dwelling older adults, high-certainty; USPSTF grade B; NICE recommends balance and strength training.

claims.claim: The whooping cough vaccine given during pregnancy protects newborns
claims.basis: CDC/ACIP and WHO: maternal Tdap in pregnancy is roughly 70 to 90% effective against infant whooping cough in the first months, consistent across meta-analyses of cohort and case-control studies.

claims.claim: Oral rehydration solution treats dehydration from diarrhea in children
claims.basis: WHO/UNICEF first-line treatment; Cochrane (Hartling 2006): oral rehydration is as effective as intravenous fluids for children with mild to moderate dehydration from gastroenteritis.

claims.claim: The flu shot can give you the flu
claims.basis: CDC: injected flu vaccines contain inactivated virus or no virus and cannot cause influenza; placebo-controlled trials in Cochrane (Demicheli 2018) show protection and only mild, short-lived soreness or low fever.

claims.claim: Daily aspirin prevents heart attacks in healthy older adults
claims.basis: ASPREE (2018): no fewer cardiovascular events in healthy adults 70 and over, more major bleeding; USPSTF 2022 grade D against starting aspirin for prevention at 60 and over.

claims.claim: Alcohol before bed helps you sleep better
claims.basis: Ebrahim 2013 systematic review and NIAAA: alcohol may shorten time to fall asleep but fragments sleep in the second half of the night and cuts REM sleep, so overall sleep quality is worse.

claims.claim: Ginkgo biloba prevents dementia
claims.basis: GEM trial (DeKosky 2008, 3,069 adults 75 and over, 6 years) and GuidAge (2012): no reduction in dementia; Cochrane (Birks 2009): evidence of benefit is inconsistent and unreliable.

claims.claim: Giving a child paracetamol for a fever prevents febrile seizures
claims.basis: Cochrane (Offringa 2017) and meta-analysis (Rosenbloom 2013): fever medicine does not prevent febrile seizures; NICE fever in under 5s says not to give it just to prevent them.

claims.claim: Soy foods raise the risk of breast cancer
claims.basis: Pooled cohort analyses and meta-analyses (Chen 2014, Nechuta 2012): soy food intake is linked to lower or unchanged breast cancer risk, not higher; ACS and AICR consider soy foods safe.

claims.claim: Apricot seeds cure cancer
claims.basis: NCI: laetrile/amygdalin showed no benefit in clinical trials (Moertel 1982) and can cause cyanide poisoning; Cochrane (Milazzo 2015): no sound evidence of benefit.

claims.claim: Talcum powder causes ovarian cancer
claims.basis: IARC rates perineal talc possibly carcinogenic (2B); case-control meta-analyses find about 20 to 30% higher odds, but large cohorts (WHI, Sister Study, pooled cohorts 2020) find no clear link; NCI calls the evidence inconsistent.

claims.claim: PSA screening saves lives
claims.basis: USPSTF 2018 grade C at 55 to 69 (individual decision) and D at 70 and over; ERSPC shows a small cut in prostate cancer deaths, PLCO shows none; Cochrane (Ilic 2013): no clear benefit, with overdiagnosis and treatment harms.

claims.claim: Cranberry juice prevents urinary tract infections
claims.basis: Cochrane (Williams 2023): cranberry products lower infection risk in women with recurrent UTIs and in children, but not clearly in older people in care homes, pregnant women or people with bladder dysfunction.

claims.claim: Hearing aids lower the risk of dementia
claims.basis: Lancet Commission lists hearing loss as a major modifiable risk factor from observational studies; ACHIEVE trial (Lin 2023) found no slowing of 3-year cognitive decline overall, only in an exploratory higher-risk subgroup.

claims.claim: Calcium supplements prevent fractures in older adults
claims.basis: USPSTF 2018 recommends against low-dose calcium plus vitamin D for fracture prevention in community-dwelling postmenopausal women (grade D); Cochrane (Avenell 2014): with vitamin D it lowers hip fractures mainly in people living in care homes.

claims.claim: Sea moss boosts your immune system
claims.basis: No human trial of sea moss on infections or immune outcomes; only lab and animal work on carrageenan and algae extracts.

claims.claim: Amber necklaces ease teething pain
claims.basis: No controlled study in babies; AAP and the Canadian Paediatric Society find no evidence of benefit and warn of strangulation and choking.

claims.claim: BPC-157 speeds up injury healing
claims.basis: A 2025 systematic review of orthopaedic use found almost all studies were in animals, with a single small human study and no controlled human trials; banned by WADA, not approved as a drug.
